title: Day 21 — Sliding-Window Maximum
prompt: We report the max latency over the last W samples at every position in a long stream. The current code recomputes each window's max from scratch and can't keep up. Same output — how would you speed it up?

clarifications.answer: Output must be identical — the max of every contiguous window of size W, left to right. Only the speed changes.
Current is O(n*W). Target O(n) — amortized linear.
1 <= W <= len(nums). W <= 0 raises ValueError. Empty input returns [].
A monotonic deque of indices is the intended structure — the front holds the current max.
O(W) extra space for the deque is expected and fine.
Equal values are fine; popping strictly-smaller-or-equal from the back keeps it correct.

hints: When the window slides by one, what did the previous window already tell you that you're throwing away?
Keep a deque of INDICES whose values are decreasing. The front is always the max of the current window.
For each i: pop from the back while nums[back] <= nums[i]; push i; pop the front if it's left the window (front <= i-W); once i >= W-1, record nums[front].
